stories.title: IWG/Regus Leases Two Floors at Cohen Brothers’ 475 Park Ave. South
stories.excerpt: Charles S. Cohen, chairman and CEO of Cohen Brothers Realty Corporation, on Tuesday announced five recent leasing transactions at 475 Park Ave. South in Manhattan. The largest of the leases was a 22,000-square-foot lease with International Workplace Group (IWG), the parent company of Regus (RGN), covering the entire 26th and 27th floors of the 35-story Midtown South tower. The new location will allow IWG/Regus to expand its presence in Midtown South. The IWG lease is joined by four additional transactions completed in recent months — a new lease, an expansion, and two renewals — reflecting sustained tenant demand at the recently transformed office property. T.J. Hochanadel and Will Propst of JLL represented IWG/Regus, while Adam Foster of CBRE and Marc Horowitz of Cohen Brothers Realty Corporation represented the landlord. Other leases completed recently at 475 PAS included Millennium Alliance expanding and extending to 20,020 square feet, represented by Taylor Scheinman of CBRE; CRC North signing a new lease of approximately 4,000 square feet, represented by Michael Hymowitz of LSL Advisors, together with Glenn Isaacson and Tony Builder of Bradford Allen; Contour Venture Partners renewing its 3,300-square-foot lease for three and a half years; and Starbucks renewing its 1,550-square-foot ground-floor space, represented by David Firestein of TSCG. The post IWG/Regus Leases Two Floors at Cohen Brothers’ 475 Park Ave. South appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IWG/Regus leases 22,000 SF (floors 26-27) at 475 Park Ave South, Manhattan Midtown South.
Five total transactions closed recently; sustained office tenant demand at renovated property.
Regus expansion signals continued coworking/flex-space adoption in prime Manhattan office markets.
stories.summary: International Workplace Group (Regus parent) signed a 22,000-square-foot lease for two full floors at 475 Park Ave. South in Midtown South, joined by four additional leasing transactions (expansions and renewals totaling ~29k SF) at the recently transformed 35-story tower. The deal demonstrates resilience in Manhattan office leasing despite broader sector headwinds.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. Office-space leasing velocity and tenant confidence in Midtown South may eventually support residential demand in the submarket, but this is a secondary signal; the article reflects office market activity, not residential demand drivers or supply constraints.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Closes Suburban Chicago Multifamily Property Sale
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of a 220-unit multifamily asset in St. Charles, Illinois.“Located in a high-demand submarket, Fox Run Apartments is a fully renovated asset well-positioned for long-term growth,” said Ryan D. Engle, senior managing director of investments in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook office. Engle and Andrean Angelov of Marcus & Millichap had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller, a private investor, and procured the buyer, also a private investor.The property is accessible from Illinois Route 38 and Route 64, a short drive from the Geneva Metra commuter rail station, and within walking distance of public transportation. The downtown Chicago Loop and O’Hare International Airport are 45 and 30 miles away, respectively. Built in 1973 on 7.5 acres at 115 Walnut Drive, Fox Run Apartments has loft-style apartments with updated kitchens and stainless-steel appliances. bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 220-unit Fox Run Apartments in St. Charles, Illinois suburban Chicago.
Fully renovated asset on 7.5 acres; buyer and seller both private investors.
Property 30 miles from O'Hare, near Metra rail access; high-demand submarket per broker.
stories.summary: A 220-unit multifamily property (built 1973, recently renovated with loft-style units) in St. Charles sold via Marcus & Millichap to a private investor. The asset is positioned near commuter rail (Geneva Metra) and major transport corridors, in a submarket the broker characterized as high-demand with long-term growth potential.
stories.impact: Asset sale velocity in suburban Chicago's western corridor (St. Charles/Geneva Metra shed) reflects continued investor appetite for renovated workforce housing near transit. St. Charles remains attractive for hold-and-stabilize plays; limited signal on new development feasibility absent cap-rate or financing detail, but transaction confirms market liquidity and interest in transit-adjacent suburban infill.

stories.title: WNC Closes on 23rd California-Focused Affordable Housing Fund
stories.excerpt: WNC & Associates, Inc. has closed on WNC Institutional Tax Credit Fund X California Series 23, L.P. The $66.3-million fund is the company’s 23rd consecutive California-focused multi-investor affordable housing fund for institutional investors.  CA23 includes six new-construction affordable housing properties totaling 650 homes across Los Angeles, San Benito and San Diego counties, Financing from the fund will help four developers bring their projects to completion. All six properties will serve families and utilize 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. “Closing CA23 is an important milestone for WNC as we celebrate our 55th year of operations” said Will Cooper Jr., president and CEO of WNC. “We are proud of our California roots and the role our home state has played in WNC’s growth into a national affordable housing organization.” The Irvine-based company has sponsored 41 California-focused funds and invested in 350 properties across 180 communities in the state, in addition to its national footprint. bullets: WNC closed $66.3M tax-credit fund (CA23) for 650 new affordable units across CA.

stories.summary: WNC & Associates closed its 23rd consecutive California-focused affordable housing fund at $66.3 million, financing six new-construction properties totaling 650 homes across Los Angeles, San Benito, and San Diego counties. All projects utilize 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to serve families; the fund marks WNC's milestone 55th anniversary and reinforces its position as a dominant LIHTC syndicator in California.
stories.impact: Sustained capital availability for affordable new construction in Southern California (LA, San Diego) signals strong LIHTC market demand and institutional investor appetite for tax-credit equity. For market-rate developers, this indicates robust public-subsidy competition for housing sites in LA and San Diego; affordable deals will absorb prime land and may suppress market-rate development feasibility in tight submarkets. Monitor LIHTC equity pricing and fund oversubscription as a leading indicator of developer competition intensity.

stories.title: Berkadia Secures $12M in LIHTC Equity for Michigan Housing Property
stories.excerpt: Berkadia secured financing for Lighthouse Ridge Apartments, a 52-unit garden-style multifamily property in South Haven, Michigan. Associate Director James Grande of Berkadia Affordable Housing led the Berkadia team in securing $12.4 million in LIHTC equity on behalf of the developer, Wallick Development, in partnership with Bogan Developments and Mno-Bmadsen. The deal marks Berkadia’s first closing with Wallick. “Lighthouse Ridge Apartments is a meaningful project for the South Haven market,” said Grande. “This investment supports the creation of new housing options that will benefit the broader community for years to come.” Once complete, the community will include 40 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom units housed in three buildings. It will also include a separate clubhouse, which will house the community space, management office, laundry room, fitness center and business center. bullets: Berkadia secured $12.4M LIHTC equity for 52-unit Lighthouse Ridge Apartments in South Haven, Michigan.
Garden-style property (40 two-bed, 12 three-bed units) in three buildings with clubhouse amenities.

stories.summary: Berkadia Affordable Housing arranged $12.4 million in LIHTC equity financing for Lighthouse Ridge Apartments, a 52-unit new-construction project in South Haven, Michigan, developed by Wallick Development in partnership with Bogan Developments and Mno-Bmadsen. The property will include three garden-style buildings, a clubhouse with fitness and community facilities, and will serve the local South Haven housing market.
stories.impact: LIHTC capital flowing to secondary markets (South Haven, MI) indicates continued lender/syndicator appetite for smaller-scale affordable development outside Tier-1 metros. For regional developers, this signals sustainable tax-credit financing for workforce housing; for market-rate builders, affordable projects in secondary metros face less crowded capital competition but also lower rents—monitor affordability-to-market-rate rent ratios to assess market-rate demand elasticity in such locations.

stories.title: Acadia Buys Mixed-Use Property on SoHo’s Greene Street for $60M
stories.excerpt: Acadia Realty Trust has snapped up a mixed-use property on SoHo’s Greene Street. The real estate investment trust (REIT) purchased two interconnected buildings at 69 Greene Street and 71-73 Greene Street from New York City-based property investment firm JSRE Acquisitions for a combined $60 million, according to city records made public Tuesday. The deal was completed in two separate transactions. Using the entity 69 Greene Owner, Acadia bought the five-story residential and retail building at 69 Greene Street for $29.4 million, while the REIT used the LLC 71-73 Greene Owner to acquire the five-story residential and retail property at 71-73 Greene Street for $30.6 million, records show. Streetwear boutique Amiri is currently a retail tenant at the base of the property. The properties last sold for $33 million in 2012. JSRE, which is affiliated with the billionaire Safra family, used similarly named entities in the transactions. Carlos Bertaco and Gina Sutt Malul signed the deals for JSRE, while Jason Blacksberg, executive vice president and chief legal officer at Acadia, signed for the buyer, according to records. It’s unclear who brokered the new deal. A spokesperson for Acadia did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while a spokesperson for JSRE could not be reached for comment. The deal represents Acadia’s continued interest in retail properties along Greene Street after buying the Givenchy-anchored retail condo at 92 and 94 Greene Street from Continental Ventures for $44 million in October 2024, as Commercial Observer previously reported. Also in SoHo, the REIT bought the Moschino-anchored retail condo at 73 Wooster Street for $25 million in January 2025. But Acadia seems focused on retail investments in general across New York City. In February, it acquired four storefronts along Madison Avenue on Manhattan’s Upper East Side from Naftali Group for a total of $20.7 million. bullets: Acadia Realty Trust acquired two mixed-use buildings at 69 and 71-73 Greene Street, SoHo, for $60M.
Two separate transactions: $29.4M (69 Greene) and $30.6M (71-73 Greene); five-story residential-retail.

stories.summary: Acadia Realty Trust purchased two interconnected mixed-use buildings on SoHo's Greene Street for a combined $60 million—$29.4 million for 69 Greene Street and $30.6 million for 71-73 Greene Street—from JSRE Acquisitions. Both five-story buildings combine residential units with street-level retail (anchored by Amiri); the properties last traded for $33 million in 2012, reflecting significant appreciation.
stories.impact: REIT acquisition of SoHo mixed-use assets signals continued institutional capital into Manhattan residential, particularly trophy/historic neighborhoods with strong tourism and retail appeal. For development teams, Acadia's SoHo-focused activity may intensify land and development-site competition in Manhattan; existing housing supply in SoHo remains constrained by historic preservation and small-lot fragmentation, limiting new supply and supporting rent resilience—monitor Acadia's Manhattan strategy as indicator of REIT confidence in NYC multifamily fundamentals and capital deployment pace.

stories.title: GAIA Lands One-Year Extension on Williamsburg Multifamily Loan
stories.excerpt: GAIA Real Estate has secured an additional one-year extension of its $48-million loan with Raymond James Bank for 55 Hope, a 117-unit multifamily property in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The extension pushes the loan’s maturity to August 2027. “We are pleased to continue our partnership with Raymond James at 55 Hope,” said Danny Fishman, CEO and co-founder, GAIA Real Estate. “We acquired the property at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, amid significant uncertainty in New York, and have since increased net operating income significantly through active management and a long-term approach to value creation. This extension demonstrates our ability to identify opportunities across market cycles and position our investments for sustained performance in Brooklyn’s multifamily market.” Originally built as a pencil factory, 55 Hope was gut-renovated in 2012 into condo-style apartments. Since its inception, GAIA Real Estate has acquired more than 20,000 residential units and managed approximately $4 billion in assets. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: GAIA Real Estate secured one-year extension on $48M Raymond James Bank loan for 55 Hope, Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

stories.summary: GAIA Real Estate obtained a one-year extension on its $48 million loan from Raymond James Bank for 55 Hope, a 117-unit condo-style multifamily property in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, extending maturity to August 2027. GAIA acquired the asset (gut-renovated from a pencil factory in 2012) during the COVID-19 pandemic and has achieved material NOI growth through active management and value-add operations.
stories.impact: Successful loan extension signals lender confidence in Brooklyn Williamsburg multifamily fundamentals and GAIA's operational track record; no refinance distress despite prior pandemic-era uncertainty. For developers, this confirms rental market stability and lender appetite for Williamsburg hold/stabilize positions; the 2027 maturity also indicates potential exit/refinance activity in 2026–27, which may accelerate cap-rate compression or prompt sales as institutional owners rebalance. Monitor similar extensions across NYC portfolio lenders as harbinger of refinance/exit timing.

stories.title: Women’s Clothing Store Esti’s Takes 8K SF at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood
stories.excerpt: High-end women’s clothing store Esti’s is relocating to a new mixed-use development in Midwood, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The longtime retailer’s 7,800-square-foot lease at 2263 Nostrand Avenue was signed on Tuesday. Asking rent for the 10-year deal was $65 per square foot. The retail space at the corner of Nostrand Avenue and Avenue I occupies a large slice of the newly constructed property’s retail component, leaving just 2,700 square feet available. The 67-unit mixed-use building was completed last year by developer Steven Hurwitz’s CAVU Property Group. Esti’s planned relocation will bring the retailer 2.1 miles northward from its current storefront at 2067 Coney Island Avenue in Brooklyn’s Homecrest neighborhood. Ownership plans to take occupancy at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in the first quarter of 2027, according to the landlord’s brokers. CAVU Property Group — the name is an acronym for Ceiling and Visibility Unlimited — was represented by MOD Commercial Realty’s Eddie Mamiye, Meyer Dagmy and Isaac Bijou, while Momentum Realty Group’s Solomon Betesh, Jonathan Lib and Avi Akiva negotiated on behalf of Esti’s. “I’ve been looking for spaces for Esti’s for about four or five months, and finally found them the perfect match at this address,” Betesh told CO. The nearly 8,000-square-foot space was a rare find for the retailer, Betesh added, particularly in South Brooklyn’s Midwood neighborhood, which remains largely residential. Esti’s ownership declined to comment on the deal. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: High-end women's clothing retailer Esti's signed 7,800 SF retail lease at 2263 Nostrand Ave, Midwood, Brooklyn.
10-year lease at $65/SF asking rent; occupancy Q1 2027 in 67-unit mixed-use building by CAVU Property Group.
Relocation 2.1 miles north from Homecrest; leaves only 2,700 SF retail vacant in newly completed property.
stories.summary: Esti's, a longstanding high-end women's clothing retailer, signed a 7,800-square-foot, 10-year lease at $65 per square foot in the newly constructed 67-unit mixed-use building at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood, Brooklyn. The relocation, occurring in Q1 2027, represents northward expansion from its current Homecrest location and nearly fills the property's retail component, leaving only 2,700 SF unleased.
stories.impact: Strong retail leasing (near full occupancy) in new Midwood mixed-use development signals robust ground-floor demand and developer confidence in neighborhood foot traffic/retail economics. For multifamily developers, this validates mixed-use development feasibility in Brooklyn's emerging neighborhoods; retail strength supports residential NOI and lender comfort with mixed-use pro formas. Monitor Midwood's retail-to-residential leasing velocity as Nostrand Ave gentrifies; rising rents and retail demand may indicate resident demographic shift toward higher-income households.

stories.title: New York Life Provides $54M Refi for California Self-Storage Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Investec Real Estate Companies has secured $53.5 million to refinance a portfolio of three self-storage assets in Central and Southern California that span 253,496 rentable square feet and hold 1,818 units, according to a release. New York Life provided the debt, structured as a five-year, full-term, interest-only loan, while Talonvest Capital’s Andrew Marshall, Kim Bishop, Mason Brusseau and Lauren Maehler arranged the transaction. Kenny Slaught, president of Investec Real Estate, praised Talonvest Capital in a statement and noted that the financing deal saved his firm $400,000 in interest over the loan term. Slaught added that the loan includes an early rate lock, protecting Investec from any interest rate changes that occur prior to closing. “Talonvest understood our objectives, identified the right capital source, and delivered a loan that exceeded our expectations,” Slaught said. “Their capital markets expertise and ability to negotiate superior terms created meaningful value for our portfolio.” The three self-storage assets are in the California cities of Highland, Goleta and Murrieta. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: New York Life provided $53.5M refinance for Investec Real Estate's three-property self-storage portfolio in California.
Portfolio: 253,496 SF, 1,818 units across Central and Southern California; five-year, interest-only structure.
Talonvest Capital brokered deal; $400K interest savings; early rate lock feature included.
stories.summary: New York Life structured a $53.5 million, five-year, interest-only refinance loan for Investec Real Estate's three-asset self-storage portfolio spanning 253,496 rentable square feet and 1,818 units in Central and Southern California. Talonvest Capital arranged the transaction, which included an early rate lock and delivered $400,000 in interest savings versus comparable alternatives.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Self-storage refi activity reflects broader CRE capital market function and lender appetite for alternative real estate classes; indicates institutional debt availability but does not signal residential demand, supply, or development feasibility changes. Self-storage and multifamily may compete for development sites in tight California markets—monitor land availability and cost trends as secondary signal.

stories.title: Electrical Contractor L.K. Comstock Signs 14K-SF Lease at Dumbo Heights Campus
stories.excerpt: This Dumbo, Brooklyn, office property is about to light up with a new tenant. L.K. Comstock, a specialty electrical contractor focused on transit rail systems, has signed a 13,566-square-foot lease at 55 Prospect Street in the office and mixed-use campus known as Dumbo Heights, Commercial Observer has learned. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood was $53 per square foot as of May, according to The New York Times. L.K. Comstock will occupy space on the third and eighth floors of 55 Prospect Street, one of several interconnected buildings at Dumbo Heights, which is owned by a joint venture of RFR and Kushner Companies. Other buildings in the campus include 77 Sands Street and 117 Adams Street. This is a new location for L.K. Comstock, which lists the headquarters for its affiliated RailWorks Corporation at 5 Penn Plaza on its website. Its new spot at 55 Prospect Street will act as a field office for the firm while it works on a nearby infrastructure project. “We were able to attract this tenant due to our close proximity to the subway lines they will be working on, as well as the turnkey, move-in-ready spaces available at the campus,” ABS Partners Real Estate’s Ben Waller, who represented the landlord alongside Daria Ghasemi and Zoe Snow, said in a statement. The tenant was represented by Avison Young’s Joe Gervino and Alexis Odgers. A spokesperson for Avison Young did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. The Dumbo Heights campus is a 750,000-square-foot development featuring office space, dining and retail, located between the Manhattan Bridge and Brooklyn Bridge. Other tenants at the campus include general contractor ETC Companies and creative agency Futerra, which both signed deals there in February. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: L.K. Comstock, electrical contractor, signed 13,566 SF lease at 55 Prospect Street, Dumbo Heights, Brooklyn.
Third and eighth floor spaces in mixed-use campus owned by RFR and Kushner Companies joint venture.
Brooklyn Dumbo office asking rents ~$53/SF as of May; new tenant headquarters relocation.
stories.summary: L.K. Comstock, a specialty electrical contractor serving transit rail systems, leased 13,566 square feet across two floors at 55 Prospect Street in the Dumbo Heights mixed-use campus (jointly owned by RFR and Kushner Companies). The lease marks a new headquarters location for the company and follows Dumbo's broader office market recovery, with asking rents averaging ~$53 per square foot.
stories.impact: Office leasing in Dumbo Heights (RFR/Kushner JV) reflects continued institutional capital deployment in Brooklyn office and mixed-use; does not directly impact multifamily fundamentals. Dumbo's office resilience may support mixed-use residential components and residential spillover demand (workers commuting/living in Brooklyn), but signal is indirect and relies on office market recovery continuation.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Supplies $93M C-PACE Loan for Cleveland Office Conversion to W Hotel
stories.excerpt: The increased utilization of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) debt for conversion projects has reached new heights with Cleveland’s fifth-tallest building. ErieView Development has secured a $93.4 million C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital (NGC) to transform the former Erieview Tower building in Downtown Cleveland into Ohio’s first W Hotel, according to the lender. The developer will also be offering apartments and office space on the building’s upper floors as part of the large-scale redevelopment. Chris Ellis, senior director of originations at NGC, said the deal announced Tuesday highlights how C-PACE financing can be used in the capital stack for a variety of CRE projects, especially office conversions. Ellis noted that the borrower opted to deploy the maximum amount of allowable C-PACE proceeds under Ohio law to save costs and avoid a future refinance. “C-PACE can be particularly beneficial for adaptive reuse projects like this one, since older buildings being converted to new uses often fall short of current energy codes and have more components that need to be updated,” Ellis told Commercial Observer. “This, in turn, creates a larger pool of costs eligible for C-PACE’s accretive financing.” Ellis said the deal marks the largest C-PACE transaction closed in Ohio to date. He added that going forward C-PACE can remain an effective financing tool for adaptive reuse projects at aging commercial buildings across the Midwest in cities like Cleveland, Columbus, Chicago, Detroit and Minneapolis. In addition to the C-PACE loan, ErieView Development also landed $20 million of senior financing from CNB Bank for the project. It also received $104.6 million of funding from a combination of equity sources, bridge loans against tax credits granted for maintaining historical aspects of the building, a loan from Cuyahoga County and incentives from the Cleveland-Cuyahoga County Port Authority, according to Ellis. bullets: Nuveen Green Capital provided $93.4M C-PACE loan to ErieView Development for Erieview Tower Cleveland conversion.
Former office tower to W Hotel plus apartments and office on upper floors; Ohio first W Hotel.

stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital structured a $93.4 million Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) loan to finance ErieView Development's conversion of Cleveland's Erieview Tower into Ohio's first W Hotel, with apartments and office space on upper floors. The developer maximized C-PACE proceeds under Ohio statute to optimize capital structure and avoid future refinancing.
stories.impact: C-PACE adaptive-reuse financing growth signals alternative capital sources for office-to-residential conversions, especially in secondary markets (Cleveland). For multifamily developers, C-PACE availability expands feasibility for obsolete office conversions in downtowns with weak office demand; however, residential units in hotel-office conversions are often boutique/limited supply. Monitor C-PACE market expansion and pricing as it may increase competition for conversion deals and accelerate office-to-multifamily pipelines in distressed Midwest and Northeast office markets—critical leading indicator of future residential supply in secondary markets.
